episodes.152425: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed ahead of a strong cold front.
episodes.152687: A nearby front and upper air troughs generated periods of heavy rain across Oahu and Kauai. The precipitation caused ponding on roadways, and small stream and drainage ditch flooding. No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.153047: Tropical Depression 28 over the western Caribbean, which eventually became Hurricane  Zeta, helped to provide copious tropical moisture over South Florida. As an upper level trough traversed aloft, additional deep moisture overspread the South Florida ahead of an approaching frontal boundary. This resulted in widespread rainfall over several days that lead to significant flooding across the east coast metro areas, which had already received several inches of rainfall from previous days. ||The most impactful flooding occurred in Palm Beach County where several neighborhoods across the county experienced major street and field flooding, and several homes had water intrusion. The flooding lingered for several days in some of these areas.
episodes.153290: Slow moving thunderstorms over the Panama City area resulted in 2 to 3 inches of rain falling in just 1 hour.  Several roads were flooded.
episodes.153293: Strong thunderstorms along the Bay and Gulf county coasts produced measured wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.153461: Strong thunderstorms produced strong winds across portion of the western Florida Panhandle coastal waters.
episodes.153505: As a shortwave trough moved across the Lower Mississippi Valley region on the evening of October 23, a broken line of thunderstorms developed and moved through Mississippi. Isolated damaging wind gusts occurred with a few of the stronger thunderstorms.
episodes.153583: A strong cold front moved through the Mid-South during the late afternoon and early evening hours on October 23rd. The front interacted with some marginal instability and scattered showers and thunderstorms developed resulting in locally heavy rain. Flash flooding occurred in Tupelo.
episodes.153693: A strong cold front approached the area subsequent to record heat across western New York. A pre-frontal trough ignited thunderstorms upstream from lower Michigan through northern Ohio. Thunderstorms overall diminished as they moved toward the area late in the evening. Though not impressive in terms of reflectivity and lightning produced, an isolated cell moving toward shore near Buffalo and produced a 62 mph wind gust. Stronger environmental winds from the large scale were likely funneled down the lake and brought to the surface due to the weak convection. An additional later report of some damage at a marina came from the Lake Ontario shoreline as convection moved farther inland in Wilson.
episodes.153731: A short wave and a weak cold front moved into the region allowing scattered showers and storms to develop. Heavy rain moved across Iberia Parish which caused isolated flash flooding.
episodes.153811: A generally light-rain, wedge set up for the state of Georgia caused localized flash flooding in the city of Atlanta as rain focused and trained over the area. Rainfall amounts of 2.5 to 5 inches were common in the Cobb, Fulton, DeKalb and Gwinnett counties, with Fulton reporting water entering buildings and a couple water rescues.
